questions.question: What situation, reported from Ibn Abbas and recorded by Imam Tabari, prompted the revelation of the rebuke in verse 2?
options: Some believers claimed in battle to have struck enemies and shown courage when they had actually retreated or been absent
A group of Companions publicly denied that jihad was an obligation
Certain hypocrites of Medina spread false rumours about the Prophet's family
Some believers refused to attend the Friday prayer while claiming to be observant Muslims
questions.explanation: Imam Tabari records in Jami al-Bayan, from multiple chains including Ibn Abbas, that some Muslims boasted of martial exploits they had not performed — claiming to have struck enemies and broken spears in battles where they had in fact fled or stayed away. The rhetorical question 'Why do you say what you do not do?' was revealed as both rebuke and reminder.

questions.question: True or false: Imam al-Qurtubi, in Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran, connects verse 3 to a hadith in Sahih Muslim about a man whose intestines unravel in the Fire because he used to command good without practising it.
questions.explanation: Qurtubi does cite this hadith from Sahih Muslim in his commentary on verse 3, presenting it as the prophetic commentary on the verse's condemnation. The hadith describes a man brought on the Day of Resurrection and cast into the Fire, and the people of the Fire recognise him as one who used to command good but not do it and forbid evil but commit it himself.

questions.question: Verse 4 declares that Allah loves those who fight in His cause standing in ranks 'like a solid, cemented structure.' What does the name of this surah — As-Saf — mean?
options: The Victory
The Ranks
The Covenant
The Light
questions.explanation: The word 'saffan' (ranks) in this verse gives the surah its name: As-Saf, meaning The Ranks. The tafsir explains that the image of 'bunyan marsus' — a cemented structure in which the joints are sealed so no gaps remain — was understood by the Companions to describe the disciplined, gap-free battle lines the Prophet arranged before engagement.

questions.question: True or false: Verse 5 states that the Children of Israel harmed Musa out of genuine ignorance of his prophetic status.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly includes the phrase 'wa qad ta'lamuna' — 'when you certainly know' that I am the Messenger of Allah. This intensifies the indictment: their harm arose from deliberate, knowing rejection, not ignorance. The tafsir presents this as the archetype of a community that failed its prophet despite possessing clear knowledge of his status.

questions.question: Which principle of theology does Imam al-Qurtubi derive from the phrase 'fa lamma zaghu azagha Allahu qulubahum' — 'when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate' — in verse 5?
options: That Allah predetermines sin before human beings make any choice
That divine misguidance is an arbitrary act unrelated to human behaviour
That the hardening of the heart is Allah's just response to prior human deviation, consistent with His attribute of Al-Hakim
That only the Children of Israel are subject to this spiritual law
questions.explanation: Qurtubi in Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran cites this verse in his discussion of divine guidance and misguidance, affirming the Sunni Ashari position that Allah's withdrawal of guidance is a just response to the servant's prior rejection, consistent with His attribute of Al-Hakim — the Wise. Human beings choose deviation first; the hardening of the heart follows as consequence, not precondition.

questions.question: In his commentary on verse 6, Ibn Kathir names several names of the Prophet Muhammad. Which of the following is among those he records from the hadith collections?
options: Al-Mustafa, Al-Mukhtar, Al-Hadi, and Al-Qadir
Muhammad, Ahmad, Al-Mahi, Al-Hashir, and Al-Aqib
Al-Amin, Al-Sadiq, Al-Bashir, and Al-Nazir
Al-Hanif, Al-Qayyim, Al-Wali, and Al-Murtada
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim records the hadith in which the Prophet declares: 'I have several names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi through whom Allah erases disbelief, I am Al-Hashir at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib after whom there will be no prophet.' This confirms Ahmad as one of the Prophet's established names.

questions.question: True or false: Sayyid Qutb, in Fi Zilal al-Quran, argues that the image of blowing out Allah's light with mouths reveals that opposition to Islam has always been primarily a war of words and rhetoric rather than purely physical force.
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb writes in Fi Zilal al-Quran that the image captures something deeply true about the psychology of opposition to Islam: it has always been primarily a war of words, narratives, and rhetoric — accusations, misrepresentations, and intellectual frameworks designed to delegitimise. The Quran's deliberate choice of 'mouths' as the instrument of opposition reflects this pattern across all eras.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir argues that the phrase 'even if the polytheists dislike it' in verse 9 carries an important instruction for Muslims engaged in dawah. What does he say this phrase rules out?
options: The use of rational arguments when presenting Islam to non-Muslims
Compromising the clarity of the Islamic message in order to avoid opposition
Engaging in dialogue with people of other faiths
Translating the Quran into languages other than Arabic
questions.explanation: Ibn Uthaymeen, drawing on this verse, emphasised that 'even if the polytheists dislike it' is a reminder to believers not to compromise the clarity of Islamic truth in order to avoid opposition — because opposition is built into the equation from the start. Al-Zuhayli similarly applies the verse to warn against diluting the message to earn social acceptance, since seeking to eliminate opposition that way defeats the purpose for which the Messenger was sent.

questions.question: The final verse commands Muslims to be 'ansarallah' — supporters of Allah. Which prophetic example does the verse hold up as the model for this commitment?
options: The companions of Musa who crossed the sea with him without hesitation
The disciples of Isa who immediately answered his call with 'We are supporters of Allah'
The believers of Mecca who endured persecution before the migration
The soldiers of Talut who crossed the river and remained firm
questions.explanation: Verse 14 recalls the hawariyin — the disciples of Isa ibn Maryam — who, when Isa asked 'Who are my supporters for Allah?', responded immediately and unconditionally: 'We are supporters of Allah.' The verse presents their swift, unhesitating commitment as the model the Muslim community is called to emulate, connecting believers to a continuous prophetic tradition of wholehearted dedication.
